answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a bridge toll paid once per crossing. New agents start with narrow limits and earn wider access only through verified completed work, so a fake swarm cannot simply appear overnight. Like a comet, a genuine reputation trail is hard to fake quickly, while cheap identities crumble like shale under scrutiny because each copy needs its own stake, history, and time. Copying an identity therefore multiplies the attacker cost instead of multiplying their influence.
